one_line: A Deccan mint master overseeing the innovative lead and copper coinage of the Satavahana era.

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, lean but sturdy build, average height
appearance.face: Oval face with warm medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, sharp arched eyebrows, a small tilak mark on the forehead, calm but focused default expression with slightly narrowed, observant eyes.
appearance.hair: Dark brown-black hair gathered into a modest topknot at the back of the crown, sides and back neatly combed; no shaved portion; simple narrow white cotton headband tied around the head with a short knot tail at the back.
appearance.costume: Knee-length off-white cotton angavastra-style upper cloth wrapped across the torso and over the left shoulder leaving the right arm free but the chest modestly covered by layered folds, paired with a plain unstitched dhoti in muted terracotta-brown wrapped to the ankles with neat pleats at the front, both in handwoven cotton with a subtle thin dark-red border; around his waist a narrow dark-indigo cotton sash functioning as a belt from which a small simple copper key-ring hangs; on his feet plain brown leather sandals; he wears a thin copper torque-style neck ornament, a single small copper earring in each ear, and a simple palm-fibre bracelet on his right wrist; over his left shoulder is also slung a rolled, slightly darker off-white cotton cloth that serves as a protective wrap when handling coin molds or tools.
appearance.signature: A shallow rectangular wooden minting tray held in his left hand containing three types of coins—dull grey lead pieces, darker potin coins, and brighter copper coins—alongside a small stone anvil and a short-handled iron punch die held in his right hand poised as if about to strike a coin.

ref_desc: A mid-30s Deccan moneyer with medium-brown skin, dark topknot and white headband, wearing off-white angavastra and terracotta dhoti with dark-indigo sash, copper ornaments and sandals, holding a wooden minting tray of lead, potin and copper coins plus stone anvil and iron punch in off-white, terracotta, indigo, lead grey and copper tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a Satavahana-era Deccan moneyer in his mid-30s with an oval medium-brown face, neat short beard, arched brows and calm, observant eyes, wearing his dark brown-black hair in a modest topknot with a narrow white cotton headband tied around his head. Show him draped in an off-white cotton angavastra-style upper cloth wrapped across his torso and over his left shoulder, covering his chest with layered folds while leaving his right arm free, paired with a plain unstitched terracotta-brown cotton dhoti wrapped neatly to his ankles with front pleats, and a dark-indigo cotton sash at his waist acting as a belt. Include a thin copper torque at his neck, one small copper earring in each ear, a simple palm-fibre bracelet on his right wrist, and plain brown leather sandals; over his left shoulder show a rolled darker off-white cotton cloth as a practical wrap. In his left hand he holds a shallow rectangular wooden minting tray containing clearly distinct dull grey lead coins, darker potin coins and brighter copper coins, alongside a small stone anvil, while in his right hand he grips a short-handled iron punch die poised as if to strike a coin. Use a restrained palette of off-white, terracotta brown, dark indigo, dull lead grey and copper red-brown, and present him from head to toe with consistent face, hair, garments, ornaments and tools in a dynamic yet dignified pose suitable for repeated redrawing.
